articles.titre: Surveillance of Sepsis in Children—Making Every Case Count
articles.extrait: [JAMA] Sepsis is a leading cause of hospital admissions, mortality, and health care expenditure worldwide. It disproportionally affects very young and very old individuals. Sepsis in young individuals carries a magnified societal impact through potential years of life lost and reductions in quality-adjusted life-years. Sepsis increases the risk of functional impairment that may persist for decades, translating into sustained health care needs and reduced lifetime economic productivity. While many countries maintain public surveillance systems for common infectious diseases such as influenza, the absence of systematic sepsis surveillance obscures the full societal burden of disease, limits benchmarking of care, and hinders effective public health measures.

articles.extrait: [www.nature.com] > If you have genuine concerns about how a colleague's mental health is affecting their ability to work don't be tempted to keep quiet out of professional loyalty. If a colleague takes you into their confidence, it's an opportunity to support them to get help, either through the practice or independently (see list below) but you should not take on sole responsibility for their mental wellbeing. If you have genuine concerns about how a colleague's mental health is affecting their ability to work don't be tempted to keep quiet out of professional loyalty. You must still raise concerns if you think patients or colleagues are at risk. Start with your practice's procedure but if that isn't possible or doesn't lead to action, seek advice from your dental defence organisation. [...] ## Reach out for help If you're worried about your own mental health, you must seek help as soon as possible from one of your colleagues, your employer and/or a healthcare professional. The GDC warns: ‘You must not rely on your own assessment of the risk you pose to patients. You should seek occupational health advice or other appropriate advice as soon as possible.'
